subject: MAP: POC environment setup dependencies (VPC, allowlists, SSO/SAML, KMS) - draft
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: POC environment setup dependencies (Draft)

Hi Alex —

Great to meet earlier. Per our discovery call, attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the POC environment setup milestone. I summarized the dependencies we discussed and proposed owners/target dates so we can unblock the POC ASAP. Please review and confirm or flag any inaccuracies.

Summary (high level):
- Goal: Stand up a short-lived POC environment for integration and perf testing by end of March.
- Primary blockers: VPC peering, IP allowlists, SSO/SAML metadata exchange, and secrets/KMS access for service keys.

Draft MAP (milestones relevant to POC env):
1) VPC peering established
   - Owner: Acme SRE / Redwood Networking (Redwood will open initial peering request and provide CIDR info)
   - Target date: 2026-03-05
   - Dependencies: Acme network ticket, firewall rules, routing table review

2) IP allowlist created for Redwood egress ranges
   - Owner: Acme SRE (template provided)
   - Target date: 2026-03-07
   - Dependencies: Confirm exact egress ranges and NAT IPs

3) SSO / SAML integration for test users
   - Owner: Acme IAM + Redwood (exchange metadata and test accounts)
   - Target date: 2026-03-12
   - Dependencies: SAML metadata, SP/IdP configuration, test account creation

4) Secrets / KMS access for POC service key
   - Owner: Acme Security + Redwood (establish key policy or use customer-managed key)
   - Target date: 2026-03-15
   - Dependencies: KMS policy, rotation window, audit access

Next steps for us:
- Action: I'll attach a MAP spreadsheet and VPC allowlist template (attached).
- Ask: Can you confirm your SRE contact and whether Acme requires us to open the peering ticket or if you will create it on your side?
- Proposed meeting: 30-min sync next Tue (2026-02-17) to finalize owners and dates if that works.

Attachments: acme-redwood-map-draft.xlsx, vpc-allowlist-template.csv

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

——
Note: MAP is intentionally concise — we can expand rows for per-task acceptance criteria after owners confirm.

Thanks Marissa — good recap and appreciate the clear milestones. A few clarifying questions before we lock dates: 

1) VPC peering: who opens the ticket? Our SRE prefers the customer (Acme) to open network change requests, but if Redwood has a formal peering request template we'll use that.
2) Allowlist ranges: can you confirm whether the ranges you provided include both TCP and UDP egress? We typically only need TCP but want to avoid surprises.
3) SAML metadata: we will validate SAML metadata exchange, but need to know whether Redwood supports metadata upload via our IdP portal or prefers a metadata file exchange.
4) KMS: what's Redwood's recommendation for POC — customer-managed key (preferred) vs Redwood-managed key?

Looping in our SRE (sre@acme.com) to coordinate on peering/allowlist. I'll also attach a short list of questions from security (attached).

Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

Thanks Alex — helpful questions. Responses inline below and I've updated the MAP spreadsheet in Drive (link below).

1) VPC peering ticket: Redwood can prepare the peering request and the exact CIDR/NAT information, but we are happy to have Acme open the formal network change ticket if that's your org's preference. Suggested approach: Redwood uploads the peering config to your ticket so your SRE has everything to triage.

2) Allowlist ranges: the attached template contains both the TCP ranges we use for API egress and the port ranges. For the POC you can restrict to TCP 443 only — that's sufficient. We'll mark that in the MAP.

3) SAML metadata exchange: Redwood supports both metadata file exchange and metadata endpoint (XML). For speed of POC, file exchange works fine — we can send our SP metadata by EOD today.

4) KMS recommendation: for production we recommend customer-managed KMS; for POC it's OK to use Redwood-managed keys if Acme prefers to avoid provisioning a key. If you need rotation policy details we can share our standard policy doc.

Updated MAP highlights (changes):
- VPC peering target moved to 2026-03-08 if Acme will open the ticket, otherwise 2026-03-05 if Redwood opens and Acme accepts.
- Allowlist target 2026-03-07 (TCP 443 only for POC)
- SAML metadata exchange target 2026-03-12 (Marissa to send SP metadata today)
- KMS decision target 2026-03-10 (Acme to confirm CSEK vs Redwood-managed)

Action items (owners):
- Marissa (Redwood): prepare peering request payload and SP metadata; update MAP spreadsheet (done) — target: today
- Acme SRE: confirm whether you will open network ticket and provide allowlist ranges — target: 2026-02-17
- Acme Security: confirm KMS decision and rotation requirements — target: 2026-03-10

Links: MAP (updated): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cMAPdraft
Peering template: attached in previous email / I've pasted the sample in the Drive doc.

If that looks good I propose we keep the meeting on Tue 02/17 10:00 PT to finalize owners. Nikhil from our infra team will be on the call to answer any networking questions.

—
Marissa Cole
